category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List four systemic metabolic risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections.
back:
- Diabetes mellitus
- Uraemia
- Jaundice
- Obesity or rapid weight loss
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5] Risk factors for increased risk of wound infection: Malnutrition (obesity, weight loss), Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice).

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does poor surgical technique specifically increase the risk of wound infection?
back:
- Creation of dead space
- Formation of haematomas
- Tissue devitalisation
- Poor haemostasis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the infection risk between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back:
- Shaving night before: Doubles SSI rate due to skin injury.
- Hair clipping: Lowest rate of infection; best method.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why does the presence of a silk suture increase the likelihood of SSI?
back:
- Acts as a foreign body
- Logarithmically reduces the critical number of organisms needed to initiate infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the 'decisive period' regarding the prevention of surgical site infections?
back:
- A 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth establishes infection.
- Prophylactic antibiotics must be present during this window.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three iatrogenic causes of reduced resistance to surgical infection.
back:
- Corticosteroids
- Chemotherapy
- Radiotherapy
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): ...iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does a prolonged preoperative hospital stay affect surgical site infection risk?
back:
- Increases risk of colonisation with MRSA.
- Increases risk of acquiring multi-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): A short preoperative hospital stay lowers the risk of acquiring MRSA, multiply resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS) and other antibiotic-resistant organisms.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Which microbial factors determine whether a surgical wound will ultimately become infected?
back:
- Virulence of the organism
- Size of the bacterial inoculum
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): The chance of developing an SSI after surgery is also determined by the pathogenicity of the organisms present and by the size of the bacterial inoculum.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Identify the local tissue health factors predisposing to surgical site infection.
back:
- Local ischaemia
- Poor vascularity
- Presence of necrotic/dead tissue
- Presence of foreign bodies
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.4] Factors that determine whether a wound will become infected: Vascularity and health of tissue... Presence of dead or foreign tissue.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List the three components of the 'cellular' host defense mechanism against infection.
back:
- Phagocytic cells (Macrophages/Polymorphonuclears)
- Killer lymphocytes
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): ...cellular: phagocytic cells, macrophages, polymorphonuclear cells and killer lymphocytes.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List three metabolic diseases that significantly increase the risk of surgical site infections (SSIs).
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5 Risk factors for increased risk of wound infection: Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How does poor surgical technique, such as creating 'dead space', predispose to infection?
back: It provides a culture medium for bacterial growth and limits the access of host defense cells to the site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Contrast the SSI risk between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back: Shaving the night before doubles SSI risk due to micro-trauma; hair clipping is the preferred method with the lowest risk.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [SSI rate... may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient on high-dose steroids for Crohn's disease presents for surgery. Why are they at higher risk for SSI?
back: Steroids cause iatrogenic immunosuppression, which impairs the inflammatory response and wound healing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids (Figures 5.4 and 5.5).]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the 'decisive period' in the context of antibiotic prophylaxis for SSI prevention?
back: The 4-hour window after tissue breach during which prophylactic antibiotics must be present to prevent established bacterial growth.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List three systemic iatrogenic factors that reduce host resistance to infection.
back:
1. Radiotherapy
2. Chemotherapy
3. Steroid therapy
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the effect of a foreign body (e.g., silk suture) on the bacterial inoculum needed for infection?
back: It logarithmically reduces the critical number of organisms required to initiate a clinical infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient with rapid weight loss and malignancy requires surgery. What nutritional state increases their SSI risk?
back: Malnutrition (even in obese patients), which weakens the host response and cellular immunity.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Which two perioperative physiological management factors are proven to reduce SSI rates in recovery?
back:
1. Avoidance of hypothermia
2. Use of supplemental oxygen
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [There is a high level of evidence that both the perioperative avoidance of hypothermia and the use of supplemental oxygen during recovery significantly reduce the rate of SSIs.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why is a long preoperative hospital stay considered a risk factor for surgical infection?
back: It increases the likelihood of colonisation with hospital-acquired resistant organisms like MRSA.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [A short preoperative hospital stay lowers the risk of acquiring MRSA... and other antibiotic-resistant organisms from the hospital environment.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List the five primary factors that determine if a wound will become infected.
back:
1. Host response
2. Pathogen virulence and inoculum size
3. Tissue vascularity/health
4. Presence of dead or foreign tissue
5. Antibiotic presence during the 'decisive period'
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.4 Factors that determine whether a wound will become infected: Host response; Virulence and inoculum of infective agent; Vascularity and health of tissue... Presence of dead or foreign tissue; Presence of antibiotics during the ‘decisive period’]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does gut failure and starvation contribute to systemic surgical infection risk?
back: Suspended enteral feeding causes bacterial translocation of aerobic gram-negative bacilli to mesenteric nodes, triggering a systemic inflammatory response (SIRS).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [When enteral feeding is suspended... bacteria (particularly aerobic gram-negative bacilli) tend to colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the infection risk between preoperative hair shaving and clipping.
back: Shaving (especially the night before) doubles the SSI rate due to skin injury/colonization; clipping immediately before surgery carries the lowest risk.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why is an obese patient with recent weight loss at high risk for SSI?
back: Recent rapid weight loss indicates malnutrition, which impairs the host inflammatory response regardless of body mass index.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis.
back: The 4-hour window after tissue breach (trauma or surgery) before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’ and strategies aimed at preventing infection... become ineffective after this time period.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Which three metabolic diseases are significant risk factors for surgical site infections?
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, uraemia and jaundice... are other contributors to infection and a poor healing response]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the microbiological effect of using silk sutures in potentially infected tissue?
back: Silk reduces the critical number of organisms needed to initiate an infection logarithmically (promoting suture abscesses).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient develops a wound infection with crepitus and brown exudate. Identify the most likely risk factor.
back: Presence of necrotic or foreign material creating anaerobic conditions for Clostridium perfringens (Gas Gangrene).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 70 (Book Page): [Gas gangrene... Patients who are immunocompromised, diabetic or have malignant disease are at greater risk, particularly if they have wounds containing necrotic or foreign material, resulting in anaerobic conditions.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How do poor surgical techniques like 'dead space' and 'haematoma' predispose to infection?
back: They create environments that protect bacterial inocula from host defenses and antibiotics, favoring suppuration.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What are the three categories of immunosuppression that increase SSI risk?
back:
1. Disease (Cancer, AIDS)
2. Steroids
3. Radiotherapy/Chemotherapy
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Immunosuppression (cancer, AIDS, steroids, chemotherapy and radiotherapy)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List the three broad determinants that govern whether a surgical wound will become infected.
back:
1. Host response (systemic factors).
2. Virulence and inoculum size of the pathogen.
3. Vascularity and health of the tissue (local factors).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [The chance of developing an SSI after surgery is also determined by the pathogenicity of the organisms present and by the size of the bacterial inoculum... Host factors are also important...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' regarding the prevention of surgical site infections.
back: The 4-hour interval after a tissue breach before bacterial growth is established enough to cause infection; prophylactic antibiotics must cover this period.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection after a breach in the tissues... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why is the use of silk sutures specifically discouraged for skin closure in surgery?
back: Silk acts as a foreign body that logarithmically reduces the critical number of organisms required to initiate an infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: An obese patient with recent 15% weight loss undergoes surgery. Which specific host factor is compromised?
back: Malnutrition; host response is weakened by rapid weight loss even if the patient is clinically obese.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Explain why preoperative skin shaving is performed immediately before surgery rather than the night before.
back: Shaving the night before causes minor skin injuries that enhance bacterial colonization, doubling the surgical site infection (SSI) rate.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [Preoperative skin shaving should be undertaken in the operating theatre immediately before surgery as the SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before, because minor skin injury enhances superficial bacterial colonisation.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List four metabolic diseases or iatrogenic treatments that reduce host resistance to infection.
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus.
2. Uraemia and jaundice.
3. Steroid therapy.
4. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, uraemia and jaundice... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Identify three local outcomes of poor surgical technique that predispose a wound to infection.
back:
1. Creation of dead space.
2. Formation of haematomas.
3. Presence of devitalised (necrotic) tissue.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: In modern practice, which is more common: endogenous or exogenous bacterial contamination? Define both.
back: Endogenous (most common) is from the patient's own flora. Exogenous is from the environment, staff, or theatre air.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): [Endogenous organisms are present on or in the patient at the time of surgery, whereas exogenous organisms come from outside the patient. In modern hospital practice, endogenous organisms colonising the patient are by far the most common source of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does suspension of enteral feeding (starvation) increase the risk of systemic infection?
back: It leads to gut failure where aerobic gram-negative bacilli colonize the upper GI tract and translocate to mesenteric nodes, releasing endotoxins.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [When enteral feeding is suspended... bacteria (particularly aerobic gram-negative bacilli) tend to colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: State the environmental factor in the operating theatre that minimizes exogenous infection risk.
back: Laminar flow systems; they direct filtered, clean air over the incision and away from the patient.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [Laminar flow systems direct clean, filtered air over the operating field, with any air potentially contaminated as it passes over the incision then directed away from the patient.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three metabolic diseases that increase the risk of surgical site infection (SSI).
back:
• Diabetes mellitus
• Uraemia
• Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, uraemia and jaundice, disseminated malignancy and acquired immmune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) are other contributors to infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does the presence of a foreign body (e.g., silk suture) affect bacterial inoculum requirements for infection?
back: It reduces the critical number of organisms needed to initiate an infection logarithmically.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the SSI risk between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back:
• Shaving: Doubles SSI rate if done the night before (due to skin micro-trauma).
• Clipping: Safest method with the lowest infection rate.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): the SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the SSI rate in a 'Dirty' wound without antibiotic prophylaxis?
back: Approximately 40%.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): Table 5.4 SSI rates... Dirty (pus or perforation, or incision through an abscess)... Infection rate without prophylaxis (%) 40.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' for antibiotic prophylaxis in surgery.
back: The 4-hour window after tissue breach before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause clinical infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection after a breach in the tissues... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three iatrogenic causes of immunosuppression that predispose to SSI.
back:
1. Radiotherapy
2. Chemotherapy
3. Steroid treatment
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): as are iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How is malnutrition clinically recognized as an SSI risk factor, even in obese patients?
back: Identified by recent rapid weight loss.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Identify three local surgical technique factors that increase the risk of infection.
back:
• Devitalised (necrotic) tissue
• Excessive dead space
• Haematoma formation
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the primary risk associated with a long preoperative hospital stay?
back: Increased risk of acquiring antibiotic-resistant organisms like MRSA and MRCNS from the hospital environment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): A short preoperative hospital stay lowers the risk of acquiring MRSA, multiply resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS) and other antibiotic-resistant organisms.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: A patient with faecal peritonitis undergoes surgery. Classify the wound and predict the infection risk without antibiotics.
back:
• Classification: Dirty
• Infection Risk: 40%
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): Dirty (pus or perforation, or incision through an abscess)... Infection rate without prophylaxis (%) 40.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three specific metabolic diseases that serve as risk factors for surgical site infections (SSIs).
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5] Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does malnutrition clinically manifest as a host response risk factor for SSI, regardless of weight?
back: It manifests as recent rapid weight loss, which can occur even in obese patients, impairing the inflammatory response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Contrast the effect of preoperative skin shaving versus hair clipping on wound infection rates.
back: Shaving the night before doubles the SSI rate due to minor skin injury; hair clipping is the superior method with the lowest infection rate.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): the SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Identify three distinct SSI risk factors in a diabetic patient on long-term steroids with a postoperative haematoma.
back:
1. Metabolic disease (Diabetes)
2. Iatrogenic immunosuppression (Steroids)
3. Poor surgical technique (Haematoma)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5] Metabolic disease (diabetes...); Immunosuppression (...steroids...); Poor surgical technique (dead space, haematoma)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the 'decisive period' for administering prophylactic antibiotics to prevent established infection?
back: The 4-hour interval after tissue breach (trauma or surgery) before bacterial growth becomes established.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Which two local tissue factors resulting from poor surgical technique increase the risk of infection?
back:
1. Excessive dead space
2. Haematoma formation
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Explain why silk sutures increase infection risk more than other materials in the skin.
back: As a foreign body, silk logarithmically reduces the critical number of organisms required to initiate a suture abscess.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does suspending enteral feeding in surgical patients predispose them to systemic infection?
back: It leads to bacterial colonization of the upper GI tract and subsequent translocation to mesenteric nodes, causing endotoxin release.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): When enteral feeding is suspended... bacteria (particularly aerobic gram-negative bacilli) tend to colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Name four iatrogenic or disease-related causes of immunosuppression that increase SSI risk.
back:
1. Radiotherapy
2. Chemotherapy
3. Steroids
4. AIDS/Cancer
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5] Immunosuppression (cancer, AIDS, steroids, chemotherapy and radiotherapy)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does the duration of preoperative hospital stay influence the risk of surgical site infections?
back: A shorter stay reduces the risk of acquiring MRSA and other antibiotic-resistant organisms from the hospital environment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): A short preoperative hospital stay lowers the risk of acquiring MRSA, multiply resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS) and other antibiotic-resistant organisms

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List four systemic host risk factors that significantly predispose a patient to surgical site infections (SSIs).
back:
1. Malnutrition (obesity or rapid weight loss).
2. Metabolic diseases (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice).
3. Immunosuppression (steroids, chemotherapy, AIDS).
4. Poor perfusion (systemic shock or local ischaemia).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5 Risk factors for increased risk of wound infection: Malnutrition, Metabolic disease, Immunosuppression, Poor perfusion...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does the presence of devitalised tissue or foreign material affect the pathogenesis of surgical infections?
back: They increase infection risk by providing a nidus for bacterial growth. Specifically, foreign bodies like silk sutures logarithmically reduce the bacterial inoculum required to initiate infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma... increase the chances of infection. If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Differentiate between Major and Minor Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) based on clinical presentation.
back:
Major SSI: Significant pus discharge, spontaneous or requiring drainage, often with systemic signs (tachycardia, pyrexia).
Minor SSI: Discharges serous fluid or small pus amounts without systemic illness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [A major SSI is defined as a wound that either discharges significant quantities of pus spontaneously or needs a secondary procedure to drain it. Minor wound infections... are not associated with excessive discomfort, systemic signs...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: A diabetic patient on chronic steroids undergoes surgery and develops an SSI. Which three risk factors are present?
back:
1. Metabolic disease (Diabetes mellitus).
2. Iatrogenic immunosuppression (Steroid therapy).
3. Impaired inflammatory/healing response due to both conditions.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus... and a poor healing response, as are iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by... steroids.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' and its relevance to the timing of prophylactic antibiotic administration.
back: The 4-hour window after tissue breach before bacterial growth establishes infection. Prophylactic antibiotics must reach tissue levels above MIC90 before this period ends (ideally at induction).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What are the four cardinal clinical features of an acute abscess as described by Celsus?
back:
1. Calor (heat).
2. Rubor (redness).
3. Dolor (pain).
4. Tumor (swelling).
*Note: Functio laesa (loss of function) is also frequently included.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [An abscess presents all the clinical features of acute inflammation originally described by Celsus: calor (heat), rubor (redness), dolor (pain) and tumor (swelling).]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Explain the relationship between preoperative skin preparation timing and the risk of wound infection.
back: Shaving the night before doubles SSI rates due to microscopic skin injuries enhancing bacterial colonization. Clipping or shaving immediately before surgery in theatre is preferred.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [Preoperative skin shaving should be undertaken in the operating theatre immediately before surgery as the SSI rate... may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Distinguish the presentation of Synergistic Spreading Gangrene (e.g., Fournier's) from simple cellulitis in surgical patients.
back: Fournier's involves polymicrobial synergy, crepitus, and extensive subdermal gangrene that far exceeds visible skin changes, usually in immunocompromised/diabetic patients.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 71 (Book Page): [The subdermal spread of gangrene is always much more extensive than appears from initial examination... Patients are almost always immunocompromised, with conditions such as diabetes mellitus.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does gut failure and starvation contribute to systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) in surgical patients?
back: Enteral suspension leads to bacterial translocation from the gut to mesenteric nodes, causing endotoxin release and a cytokine-mediated systemic inflammatory response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [When enteral feeding is suspended... bacteria... tend to colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Contrast endogenous and exogenous sources of surgical contamination.
back:
Endogenous: Organisms already present on/in the patient (most common). 
Exogenous: Acquired from the environment (theatre air, staff, non-sterile instruments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): [Endogenous organisms are present on or in the patient at the time of surgery, whereas exogenous organisms come from outside the patient.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List four major systemic host factors that increase the risk of surgical site infection.
back:
1. Malnutrition (obesity or weight loss).
2. Metabolic diseases (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice).
3. Immunosuppression (steroids, chemotherapy, AIDS).
4. Poor tissue perfusion (shock, local ischaemia).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5 Risk factors for increased risk of wound infection: Malnutrition (obesity, weight loss); Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice); Immunosuppression (cancer, AIDS, steroids, chemotherapy and radiotherapy); Poor perfusion (systemic shock or local ischaemia)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How does poor surgical technique specifically predispose a wound to infection?
back:
It creates environments conducive to bacterial growth by leaving: 
- Devitalised (dead) tissue.
- Excessive dead space.
- Haematomas (blood collections).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Contrast endogenous and exogenous sources of surgical site bacterial contamination.
back:
- Endogenous: Organisms already present on or in the patient (most common source).
- Exogenous: Organisms from outside (theatre air, staff, or unwashed hands).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): [Endogenous organisms are present on or in the patient at the time of surgery, whereas exogenous organisms come from outside the patient. In modern hospital practice, endogenous organisms colonising the patient are by far the most common source of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why is a patient on long-term steroids at higher risk for postoperative wound complications?
back: Steroids cause iatrogenic immunosuppression, which impairs the inflammatory response, weakens host resistance to pathogens, and delays the healing process.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the 'decisive period' for administering prophylactic antibiotics to prevent SSI?
back: The 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth establishes infection. Antibiotics must be present in tissues during this window to be effective.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection after a breach in the tissues... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What are the three defining clinical characteristics of a 'Major' SSI?
back:
1. Significant discharge of pus.
2. Systemic signs (pyrexia, tachycardia, raised WBC).
3. Delayed discharge or requirement for secondary drainage procedures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.6 Major wound infections: Significant quantity of pus; Delayed return home; Patients are systemically ill]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How does the timing of preoperative skin shaving influence SSI rates?
back: Shaving the night before doubles infection rates due to minor skin injuries that enhance bacterial colonisation. Shaving should be done immediately before surgery.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [Preoperative skin shaving should be undertaken in the operating theatre immediately before surgery as the SSI rate... may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why are silk sutures contraindicated for skin closure in potentially contaminated wounds?
back: Silk acts as a foreign body that logarithmically reduces the number of bacteria required to initiate a suture abscess or infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How does the presence of a prosthetic implant change the requirement for prophylactic antibiotics?
back: Prophylaxis is mandatory even in 'clean' surgery because the consequences of prosthetic infection are catastrophic, despite low baseline infection rates.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [The exception to this is where a prosthetic implant is used, as the results of infection are so catastrophic that even a small risk of infection is unacceptable.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Which two perioperative factors significantly reduce SSI rates during the recovery period?
back:
1. Maintenance of normothermia (avoiding hypothermia).
2. Administration of supplemental oxygen.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [There is a high level of evidence that both the perioperative avoidance of hypothermia and the use of supplemental oxygen during recovery significantly reduce the rate of SSIs.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three specific metabolic diseases that serve as risk factors for surgical site infections.
back:
• Diabetes mellitus
• Uraemia
• Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, uraemia and jaundice, disseminated malignancy and acquired immmune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) are other contributors to infection and a poor healing response.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does poor surgical technique physiologically predispose a wound to infection?
back:
• Creation of devitalised (necrotic) tissue
• Formation of excessive dead space
• Development of haematomas
• These environments facilitate bacterial growth.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the risk of SSI between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back:
• Shaving: Increases risk (doubles SSI rate if done the night before) due to minor skin injuries.
• Clipping: Lowest rate of infection; preferred method.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before, because minor skin injury enhances superficial bacterial colonisation... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient on long-term steroids for Crohn’s disease undergoes surgery. Identify the primary iatrogenic risk factor for SSI.
back:
• Iatrogenic immunosuppression caused by steroid therapy
• Compromised host inflammatory response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids ( Figures 5.4 and 5.5 ).]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why is the timing of prophylactic antibiotics (the 'decisive period') critical for reducing infection risk?
back:
• Antibiotics must be present during the 4-hour 'decisive period' before bacterial growth is established.
• Prophylaxis is ineffective once infection takes hold after this interval.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection after a breach in the tissues... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’ and strategies aimed at preventing infection from taking a hold become ineffective after this time period.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Which category of wound contamination carries a 40% infection risk if prophylaxis is not used?
back: • Dirty wounds (involving pus, perforated viscera, or incision through an abscess).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [Table 5.4 SSI rates... Dirty (pus or perforation, or incision through an abscess)... Infection rate without prophylaxis (%) 40]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Explain the risk associated with using silk sutures in potentially contaminated tissues.
back:
• Silk is a foreign body that logarithmically reduces the number of organisms needed to start an infection.
• Frequently leads to 'suture abscesses'.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses for this reason.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: An obese patient presents with 15% weight loss over 1 month. Why is their SSI risk increased?
back:
• Rapid weight loss indicates malnutrition regardless of obesity.
• Malnutrition weakens the host's systemic resistance and inflammatory response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does systemic shock predispose a surgical patient to wound infection?
back:
• Causes poor tissue perfusion and local ischaemia.
• Impairs the delivery of humoral and cellular defense mechanisms to the wound site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5 Risk factors... Poor perfusion (systemic shock or local ischaemia)... Summary box 5.4... Vascularity and health of tissue being invaded.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three iatrogenic treatments that reduce a patient's resistance to surgical infection.
back:
• Radiotherapy
• Chemotherapy
• Steroid administration
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List four systemic metabolic risk factors that predispose a patient to surgical site infections.
back: 1. Diabetes mellitus. 2. Uraemia. 3. Jaundice. 4. Malnutrition (including recent weight loss or obesity).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5: Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice); Malnutrition (obesity, weight loss)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does poor surgical technique specifically increase the risk of postoperative wound infection?
back: It creates devitalised tissue, excessive dead space, or haematomas, providing a medium for bacterial growth and impairing host defenses.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Differentiate between endogenous and exogenous sources of bacterial contamination in surgical wounds.
back: 1. Endogenous: Organisms already present on or in the patient (most common source). 2. Exogenous: Organisms from the environment, theatre staff, or ward.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): [Endogenous organisms are present on or in the patient at the time of surgery, whereas exogenous organisms come from outside the patient.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why are patients on long-term steroids or chemotherapy at a significantly higher risk for major SSIs?
back: These treatments cause iatrogenic immunosuppression, which weakens the host's inflammatory and healing response, often resulting in complex complications like faecal fistulas.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Reduced resistance... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the 'decisive period' for prophylactic antibiotics to prevent surgical site infections?
back: The 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth is established; antibiotics must exceed MIC90 in tissues during this window.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three local wound factors that reduce the bacterial inoculum required to initiate an infection.
back: 1. Presence of foreign bodies (e.g., sutures, drains). 2. Devitalised or necrotic tissue. 3. Local ischaemia or poor vascularity.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.4: Factors that determine whether a wound will become infected... Presence of dead or foreign tissue; Vascularity and health of tissue.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does obesity paradoxically act as a risk factor for SSI despite representing an over-nourished state?
back: It is often associated with clinical malnutrition (rapid weight loss) and poor tissue perfusion in thick adipose layers, impairing immune response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically... as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: A diabetic patient in systemic shock undergoes emergency surgery; identify the primary risk factors involved.
back: 1. Metabolic disease (Diabetes). 2. Poor perfusion (Systemic shock). 3. Impaired host response (Synergistic effect of metabolic and circulatory failure).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5: Risk factors... Metabolic disease (diabetes...); Poor perfusion (systemic shock...)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Explain how gut failure and starvation contribute to systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) in surgical patients.
back: Bacteria (aerobic gram-negative bacilli) colonize the upper GI tract and translocate to mesenteric nodes, releasing endotoxins that trigger pro-inflammatory cytokine release.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [When enteral feeding is suspended... bacteria... colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins...]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why is silk suture material contraindicated for skin closure in potentially contaminated wounds?
back: Silk acts as a foreign body that logarithmically reduces the number of organisms needed to cause infection, frequently leading to suture abscesses.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically. Silk should not be used to close skin as it causes suture abscesses.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List the specific metabolic diseases that serve as risk factors for surgical site infection (SSI).
back:
- Diabetes mellitus
- Uraemia
- Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.5] Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
coreConcept: Foreign Body Effect on Bacterial Inoculum
front: Q: How does the presence of foreign material like silk sutures increase the risk of infection?
back:
- Logarithmically reduces the critical number of organisms required to initiate an infection
- Causes suture abscesses if used to close skin
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Contrast the infection risk between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back:
- Shaving: Doubles SSI rate if done the night before (minor skin injury/colonisation)
- Clipping: Lowest rate of infection
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why are patients with Crohn's disease on high-dose steroids at extreme risk for major SSI?
back:
- Steroids cause iatrogenic immunosuppression
- Impairs the inflammatory response and host healing mechanisms
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the 'decisive period' regarding prophylactic antibiotics and infection risk?
back:
- The 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth establishes
- Antibiotics must be given before this period to be effective
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Identify the three primary host-related categories that reduce resistance to surgical infection.
back:
- Malnutrition (weight loss/obesity)
- Metabolic disease
- Immunosuppression
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by malnutrition... Metabolic diseases... and iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How do poor perfusion and systemic shock act as risk factors for wound infection?
back:
- Cause local ischaemia and reduced vascularity
- Impair the delivery of host immune cells/humoral factors to the tissue
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.4] Vascularity and health of tissue being invaded (including local ischaemia as well as systemic shock)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Why is a patient with a perforated diverticulum at significantly higher risk of SSI than one with an elective hernia repair?
back:
- Massive bacterial inoculum (endogenous source)
- Contaminated/Dirty wound classification (infection risk up to 40% without prophylaxis)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): Contamination being most severe when a hollow viscus perforates (e.g. faecal peritonitis following a diverticular perforation).

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Explain how gut failure and starvation lead to an increased risk of systemic sepsis.
back:
- Aerobic gram-negative bacilli colonise the upper GI tract
- Translocation to mesenteric nodes occurs
- Triggers release of endotoxins and proinflammatory cytokines
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Bacteria (particularly aerobic gram-negative bacilli) tend to colonise the normally sterile upper gastrointestinal tract. They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List three aspects of poor surgical technique that predispose a wound to infection.
back:
- Presence of dead space
- Formation of haematomas
- Excessive use of foreign materials/sutures
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three metabolic diseases that significantly increase the risk of surgical site infections (SSIs).
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.5] Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does gut failure/starvation during the perioperative period lead to systemic infection?
back: Bacterial colonization of the upper GI tract leads to translocation to mesenteric nodes and release of endotoxins (lipopolysaccharides).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.5] Colonisation and translocation in the gastrointestinal tract; [Text] They may then translocate to the mesenteric nodes and cause the release of endotoxins.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the SSI rates of 'Clean' vs 'Dirty' wounds when no antibiotic prophylaxis is used.
back:
Clean: 1–2%
Dirty: 40%
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [Table 5.4] Clean (no viscus opened) 1–2%; Dirty (pus or perforation) 40%

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient on long-term steroids has delayed wound healing. What is the underlying risk factor?
back: Iatrogenic immunosuppression which impairs the host inflammatory response.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.5] Immunosuppression (cancer, AIDS, steroids, chemotherapy and radiotherapy)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' for antibiotic prophylaxis and its duration.
back: The 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth establishes; antibiotics must be present in tissues during this window.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the CDC-required follow-up duration for monitoring SSIs in prosthetic surgery?
back: One year (compared to 30 days for non-prosthetic surgery).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): The US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) definition insists on a 30-day follow-up period for non-prosthetic surgery and 1 year after implanted hip and knee surgery.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Which local factors related to surgical technique increase the risk of wound infection?
back:
1. Creation of dead space
2. Presence of haematoma
3. Local ischaemia
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary Box 5.5] Poor surgical technique (dead space, haematoma)... local ischaemia

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Distinguish between endogenous and exogenous sources of surgical contamination.
back:
Endogenous: Bacteria already on/in the patient (most common).
Exogenous: Bacteria from staff, environment, or air.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): Endogenous organisms are present on or in the patient... exogenous organisms come from outside the patient.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How is malnutrition clinically identified as a risk factor for SSI, even in obese patients?
back: By recognizing recent rapid weight loss.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically... as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Why is the use of silk sutures discouraged in skin closure regarding SSI risk?
back: Foreign bodies like silk logarithmically reduce the critical number of organisms needed to initiate an infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What are the four primary determinants of whether a surgical wound will become infected?
back:
1. Host response
2. Virulence and inoculum of the infective agent
3. Vascularity and health of the tissue
4. Presence of dead or foreign tissue
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.4: Factors that determine whether a wound will become infected: Host response; Virulence and inoculum of infective agent; Vascularity and health of tissue... Presence of dead or foreign tissue]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections

back:

citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5: Risk factors for increased risk of wound infection: Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)]

back:
1. Hypothermia
2. Hypoxia (Inadequate supplemental oxygen during recovery)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [There is a high level of evidence that both the perioperative avoidance of hypothermia and the use of supplemental oxygen during recovery significantly reduce the rate of SSIs.]

back:
• Steroids

• Radiotherapy

2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5] Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How does poor surgical technique physiologically predispose a wound to infection?
back:
1. Creation of dead space
2. Formation of haematomas
3. Leaving devitalised (necrotic) tissue
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Devitalised tissue, excessive dead space or haematoma, all the results of poor surgical technique, increase the chances of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Contrast the impact of shaving versus clipping on SSI risk.
back:
1. Shaving: Shaving the night before doubles SSI rates due to skin micro-injury.
2. Clipping: Best method with the lowest rate of infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): Preoperative skin shaving should be undertaken in the operating theatre immediately before surgery as the SSI rate after clean wound surgery may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient on high-dose steroids and radiotherapy needs surgery. Why are they at higher SSI risk?
back:
1. Iatrogenic immunosuppression
2. Impaired inflammatory response
3. Delayed wound healing
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Reduced resistance to infection has several causes, particularly those that impair the inflammatory response... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by radiotherapy, chemotherapy or steroids.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the 'decisive period' for antibiotic prophylaxis and its duration?
back:
1. The 4-hour interval after tissue breach before bacterial growth is established.
2. Antibiotics must be given within this window to prevent infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection after a breach in the tissues... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: List the three natural host defense mechanisms against infection.
back:
1. Chemical: Low gastric pH
2. Humoral: Antibodies, complement, opsonins
3. Cellular: Phagocytes, macrophages, lymphocytes
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 66 (Book Page): ...chemical: low gastric pH; humoral: antibodies, complement and opsonins; cellular: phagocytic cells, macrophages, polymorphonuclear cells and killer lymphocytes.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: How do foreign bodies like silk sutures influence bacterial infection thresholds?
back: They logarithmically reduce the critical number of organisms required to initiate an infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: In a patient with gut failure, what mechanism predisposes them to SSI?
back:
1. Villous atrophy
2. Colonisation by aerobic gram-negative bacilli
3. Bacterial translocation to mesenteric nodes
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [Figure 5.6] Gut failure, colonisation and translocation related to the development of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS).

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What nutritional factors are highlighted as risks for increased wound infection?
back:
1. Malnutrition
2. Obesity
3. Recent rapid weight loss
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: What is the estimated SSI rate for 'Dirty' wounds without antibiotic prophylaxis?
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [Table 5.4] Dirty (pus or perforation, or incision through an abscess)... Infection rate without prophylaxis (%): 40

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three specific metabolic diseases that predispose a patient to surgical site infections (SSIs).
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus
2. Uraemia
3. Jaundice
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5: Metabolic disease (diabetes, uraemia, jaundice)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does malnutrition contribute to SSI risk in both thin and obese patients?
back: Recent rapid weight loss weakens the host response and impairs the inflammatory response, regardless of initial Body Mass Index (BMI).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Host response is weakened by malnutrition, which can be recognised clinically, and most easily, as recent rapid weight loss that can be present even in the presence of obesity.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Compare the SSI risk between preoperative skin shaving and hair clipping.
back: Shaving (especially the night before) doubles the SSI rate due to minor skin injuries; hair clipping immediately before surgery has the lowest infection rate.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [SSI rate... may be doubled if shaving is performed the night before... hair clipping is best, with the lowest rate of infection.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: A patient on high-dose steroids for Crohn’s disease has delayed wound healing. Why?
back: Iatrogenic immunosuppression from steroids impairs the inflammatory response and cell-mediated immunity required for wound closure and infection control.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Reduced resistance to infection has several causes, particularly those that impair the inflammatory response... iatrogenic causes including the immunosuppression caused by... steroids]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Define the 'decisive period' for prophylactic antibiotic administration.
back: The 4-hour window after tissue breach (trauma/surgery) before bacterial growth is established. Antibiotics must be present in tissues during this time.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [There is up to a 4-hour interval before bacterial growth becomes established enough to cause an infection... This interval is called the ‘decisive period’]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: List three iatrogenic/treatment-related factors that reduce host resistance to infection.
back:
1. Radiotherapy
2. Chemotherapy
3. Steroid therapy
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [Summary box 5.5: Immunosuppression (cancer, AIDS, steroids, chemotherapy and radiotherapy)]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: How does the presence of a foreign body (e.g., silk suture) affect the bacterial inoculum required for SSI?
back: Foreign bodies logarithmically reduce the critical number of organisms needed to initiate an infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 67 (Book Page): [If there is a silk suture in tissue, the critical number of organisms needed to start an infection is reduced logarithmically.]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Q: Contrast the SSI risk between a short vs. long preoperative hospital stay.
back: Longer stays increase the risk of colonisation with multidrug-resistant hospital organisms like MRSA and MRCNS.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [A short preoperative hospital stay lowers the risk of acquiring MRSA, multiply resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCNS) and other antibiotic-resistant organisms]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: What is the consequence of gut failure and starvation on systemic infection risk?
back: It leads to translocation of aerobic gram-negative bacilli to mesenteric nodes, triggering systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [In the circumstances of reduced host resistance... bacteria (particularly aerobic gram-negative bacilli) tend to colonise... then translocate to the mesenteric nodes]

category: List the common risk factors that predispose to surgical site infections
front: Identify two perioperative physiological management factors that reduce SSI rates.
back:
1. Maintenance of normothermia (avoiding hypothermia)
2. Use of supplemental oxygen during recovery
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 73 (Book Page): [There is a high level of evidence that both the perioperative avoidance of hypothermia and the use of supplemental oxygen during recovery significantly reduce the rate of SSIs.]

category: Identify early clinical features suggestive of a surgical site infection
front: Q: Name the four classical cardinal clinical features of a localized surgical site infection (SSI).
back:
1. Calor (heat)
2. Rubor (redness)
3. Dolor (pain)
4. Tumor (swelling)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [An abscess presents all the clinical features of acute inflammation originally described by Celsus: calor (heat), rubor (redness), dolor (pain) and tumor (swelling).]

category: Identify early clinical features suggestive of a surgical site infection
front: Q: Why does a localized abscess produce increasing pressure and pain?
back: Abscesses contain hyperosmolar material that draws in fluid, leading to increased internal pressure and pain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 69 (Book Page): [Abscesses contain hyperosmolar material that draws in fluid. This increases the pressure and causes pain.]

category: Identify early clinical features suggestive of a surgical site infection
front: Q: Contrast the clinical presentation of a major vs. a minor surgical site infection.
back:
Major: Significant pus, systemic illness, or needs drainage. 
Minor: Serous/minor pus discharge without systemic signs or discharge delay.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 68 (Book Page): [A major SSI is defined as a wound that either discharges significant quantities of pus... Minor wound infections may discharge pus or infected serous fluid but are not associated with excessive discomfort, systemic signs...]

category: Identify early clinical features suggestive of a surgical site infection
front: Q: A patient develops spreading wound redness and rigors 3 days post-op without pus. Suspected diagnosis?
back: Cellulitis (likely b-haemolytic streptococci), a non-suppurative invasive infection with systemic toxaemia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 74 (Book Page): [...cellulitis around wounds caused by invasive organisms (such as b-haemolytic Streptococcus) takes 3–4 days to develop.]

category: Identify early clinical features suggestive of a surgical site infection
front: Q: When are systemic antibiotics indicated following the drainage of a surgical site abscess?
back: Only if the abscess cavity is closed after drainage. If left open to heal by secondary intention, they are unnecessary.
